text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National council for environment holds second meeting on Oct 7-8.
- Privatisation Minister Abderrahman Saaidi to announce sale of 30 percent of Fertima, (Societe Marocaine des Fertilisants), the largest distributor of fertilisers in Morocco.
- Consumers worried by the increase of oil prices.
- Schools reopen while education crisis lingers and ministry's officials are involved in embezzlement of food products donated by the World Food Programme to Moroccan schools.
- Moroccan and French passengers bound for Paris blocked in Casablanca after French airline Air Liberte cancelled the flight with no previous warning.
- Environment council holds second meeting for a clean future.
- Morocco state-owned Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) and Pakistan sign accord to set up joint venture based in Karachi to produce phosphates by-products in 1998.
